text.p: Denis Compton, the golden boy of English cricket in the immediate post-war years, died in a London hospital on Tuesday night aged 78. Compton was the youngest player to score a century for England, hitting 102 against Australia at Trent Bridge in 1938.
But it was after the second World War that he was seen at his peak, scoring 3,816 for Middlesex in the 1947 season.

Handsome, debonair and often unorthodox, Compton brought a touch of glamour to the England and Middlesex sides. He scored 17 centuries in 78 matches for his country and in December, 1948, he scored the fastest-ever triple century when he hit 300 for the MCC against North-East Transvaal in 181 minutes.
His England career lasted 20 years between 1937 and 1957, with 5,807 runs came at an average of 50.06.
